items.title: The Schwarzschild exterior model datum: domain, metric, mass parameter and time orientation
items.statement:
This item assumes the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through
the manifold-product and tangent-bundle suppliers cited below
([[def-countable-choice]]); no further choice principle is used.

**(a) Parameters and the Schwarzschild radius.** Let $c>0$ and $G_N>0$ be real
constants and let $m_*>0$ be a real **mass parameter**. Put

$$s:=\frac{2G_Nm_*}{c^2}>0 .$$

The number $s$ is the **Schwarzschild radius** of the datum. Neither $c$,
$G_N$ nor $m_*$ is measured here; the physical reading of $c$ and $G_N$ as the
framework's conversion and Newton constants and of $m_*$ as a mass is fixed by
the physical conventions of the framework, not by this definition.

**(b) The underlying manifold and its product charts.** Let $S^2:=S_2(0,1)=
\{y\in\mathbb R^3:\lVert y\rVert_2=1\}$ be the unit Euclidean sphere with its
induced smooth structure ([[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]]), and let
$M$ be the product manifold

$$M:=\mathbb R\times(s,\infty)\times S^2$$

with the product smooth structure
([[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]]);
it is a smooth four-manifold without boundary. Write $x^0:M\to\mathbb R$ and
$r:M\to(s,\infty)$ for the first and second projections and $\iota:M\to S^2$
for the third. A **product chart** of $M$ is a smooth chart
$(x^0,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$ whose last two
components form a smooth chart of $S^2$ taken from the standard spherical
atlas, so that $(\vartheta,\varphi)\mapsto(\sin\vartheta\cos\varphi,
\sin\vartheta\sin\varphi,\cos\vartheta)$ is the round sphere chart, and in which
the components of the round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$ of
[[ex-the-round-metric-on-the-sphere-as-an-induced-metric]] are
$\gamma_{22}=1$, $\gamma_{23}=\gamma_{32}=0$,
$\gamma_{33}=\sin^2\vartheta$; such charts cover $M$.

**(c) The metric.** Let $f:(s,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be the smooth function

$$f(r):=1-\frac{s}{r} .$$

In every product chart define the component functions

$$g_{00}:=-f(r),\qquad g_{11}:=\frac{1}{f(r)},\qquad g_{22}:=r^2,\qquad g_{33}:=r^2\sin^2\vartheta,$$

and $g_{ab}:=0$ whenever $a\ne b$, $a,b\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, with the index order
$(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(x^0,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$. These are the components of a
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $g$ on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]): the displayed functions are
$C^\infty$ in the chart, the chart independence of the field follows from the
transformation law of the round sphere metric on overlaps of sphere charts,
and $f>0$ because $r>s$. The pair $(M,g)$ is the **Schwarzschild exterior
metric of mass parameter $m_*$**; the datum of this definition is the
quadruple $(c,G_N,m_*,g)$, equivalently the tuple $(M,g,N)$ with $N$ as in
clause (d). That $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ is not asserted here; it is proved in the companion metric-properties lemma of this page (its
justification record in the frontmatter), which also records the equivalent
coordinate-free description
$g=-f\,d(x^0)\otimes d(x^0)+f^{-1}\,dr\otimes dr+r^2\,\iota^*\gamma_{S^2}$.

**(d) Time orientation and the Schwarzschild chart.** The field
$N:=\partial_0=\partial/\partial x^0$ is smooth on $M$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); the chart components of $g$
are independent of $x^0$, so $N$ is the restriction of a global vector field,
and $g(N,N)=-f(r)<0$ at every point. The datum carries the time orientation
$N$; the product charts of clause (b) are then **Schwarzschild charts** of the
datum. We write $t$ for the coordinate $x^0/c$ when the datum is read in the
framework's unit conventions.

**(e) Scope.** The domain of the datum is the exterior region $r>s$; the
definition asserts nothing about $r=s$, about $r\le 0$, about any matter, or
about any equation satisfied by $g$. The horizon $r=s$ is not part of the
datum, and a continuation of the metric to $r=s$ requires the separate constructions recorded on this page, the
regularity lemma for the advanced chart and the Kruskal model-properties
lemma. Whether the datum is a solution of the
framework's field law is proved, not defined, in the Ricci-and-Einstein-tensor lemma of this
page.

items.title: The Schwarzschild exterior datum is a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold
items.statement:
Let $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $m_*>0$ and let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior
datum of mass parameter $m_*$ with Schwarzschild radius
$s=2G_Nm_*/c^2$ ([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]). Then:

**(a) Components and smoothness.** $M$ is a smooth four-manifold without
boundary and the assignments of component functions in the product charts of
the datum agree on overlaps and define a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $g$ on $M$, whose components in every product chart
$(x^0,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$ are

$$g_{00}=-f(r),\qquad g_{11}=\frac{1}{f(r)},\qquad g_{22}=r^2,\qquad g_{33}=r^2\sin^2\vartheta,\qquad g_{ab}=0\ (a\ne b),$$

where $f(r)=1-s/r$. Equivalently
$g=-f\,d(x^0)\otimes d(x^0)+f^{-1}\,dr\otimes dr+r^2\,\iota^*\gamma_{S^2}$,
with $\iota:M\to S^2$ the third projection and $\gamma_{S^2}$ the round
metric of the unit sphere.

**(b) Lorentzian signature.** At every $p\in M$ the form $g_p$ is
nondegenerate with inertia $(3,1,0)$; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth
Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$.

**(c) Time orientation.** The field $N=\partial_0$ is a smooth nowhere
vanishing vector field with $g_p(N_p,N_p)=-f(r(p))<0$ at every $p$; it is
therefore a time orientation of $(M,g)$, so $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented
smooth Lorentzian four-manifold. Moreover $g(\partial_0,\partial_0)=-f$ is
negative, $g(\partial_1,\partial_1)=f^{-1}$ is positive wherever $\partial_1$
is defined, and the Schwarzschild chart frame
$(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)$ is $g$-orthogonal with
$\lvert g(\partial_0,\partial_0)\rvert=f$.

**(d) Domain of the coordinates.** Every product chart is defined on a
nonempty open subset of $M$, the functions $f$, $f^{-1}$, $r$, $r^2$ and
$\sin^2\vartheta$ restricted to any chart domain are smooth, and $f(r)>0$
because $r>s$; no product chart reaches a pole of $S^2$, since the sphere
charts exclude them.

**(e) Conventions.** The identities are equalities of component functions in
each product chart and hold at every point of every chart domain; they are
not assertions about any other chart or about the physical interpretation of
the coordinates.

items.title: Christoffel symbols of the Schwarzschild exterior metric in product charts
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum of mass parameter $m_*$
with Schwarzschild radius $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2$ and
$f(r)=1-s/r$ ([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), and let $\nabla$ be
the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). In every product
chart $(x^0,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$ with $f'=\frac{df}{dr}=s/r^2$, the
Christoffel symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]) are:

**(a)** $\Gamma^0{}_{01}=\Gamma^0{}_{10}=\dfrac{f'}{2f}$, and
$\Gamma^0{}_{00}=\Gamma^0{}_{11}=\Gamma^0{}_{ij}=0$ for all remaining index
pairs;

**(b)** $\Gamma^1{}_{00}=\dfrac{ff'}{2}$,
$\Gamma^1{}_{11}=-\dfrac{f'}{2f}$, $\Gamma^1{}_{22}=-rf$,
$\Gamma^1{}_{33}=-rf\sin^2\vartheta$, and
$\Gamma^1{}_{01}=\Gamma^1{}_{02}=\Gamma^1{}_{03}=\Gamma^1{}_{12}=\Gamma^1{}_{13}=\Gamma^1{}_{23}=0$;

**(c)** $\Gamma^2{}_{12}=\Gamma^2{}_{21}=\dfrac{1}{r}$,
$\Gamma^2{}_{33}=-\sin\vartheta\cos\vartheta$, and every other symbol with
upper index $2$ vanishes;

**(d)** $\Gamma^3{}_{13}=\Gamma^3{}_{31}=\dfrac{1}{r}$,
$\Gamma^3{}_{23}=\Gamma^3{}_{32}=\cot\vartheta$, and every other symbol with
upper index $3$ vanishes.

All components not listed vanish; equivalently, the only nonzero symbols are
those displayed. For the model value $f(r)=1-s/r$, so that $f'=s/r^2$, the
listed symbols read

$$\Gamma^0{}_{01}=\Gamma^0{}_{10}=\frac{s}{2r^2 f},\qquad \Gamma^1{}_{00}=\frac{s f}{2r^2},\qquad \Gamma^1{}_{11}=-\frac{s}{2r^2f},$$

$$\Gamma^1{}_{22}=-rf,\qquad \Gamma^1{}_{33}=-rf\sin^2\vartheta,\qquad \Gamma^2{}_{12}=\Gamma^3{}_{13}=\frac{1}{r},\qquad \Gamma^2{}_{33}=-\sin\vartheta\cos\vartheta,\qquad \Gamma^3{}_{23}=\cot\vartheta .$$

items.title: Curvature components and the vanishing of the Ricci and Einstein tensors of the Schwarzschild exterior metric
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum of mass parameter $m_*$,
Schwarzschild radius $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$
([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ and curvature data $R^a{}_{bcd}$, $R_{abcd}$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$, $G_{ab}$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). In every product chart
$(x^0,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$, writing $f'=\frac{df}{dr}=s/r^2$ and
$f''=\frac{d^2f}{dr^2}=-2s/r^3$:

**(a) Curvature components.** All nonzero components of the lowered
curvature tensor, up to the symmetries of
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]], are

$$R_{0101}=\frac{f''}{2},\qquad R_{0202}=\frac{rf f'}{2},\qquad R_{0303}=\frac{rf f'\sin^2\vartheta}{2},$$

$$R_{1212}=-\frac{rf'}{2f},\qquad R_{1313}=-\frac{rf'\sin^2\vartheta}{2f},\qquad R_{2323}=r^2\bigl(1-f\bigr)\sin^2\vartheta .$$

Every component whose index pairs do not coincide as unordered pairs, and
every component with an index repeated inside a pair, vanishes.

**(b) Ricci tensor.** The Ricci tensor has the diagonal components

$$\operatorname{Ric}_{00}=f\Bigl(\frac{f''}{2}+\frac{f'}{r}\Bigr),\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{11}=-\frac{1}{f}\Bigl(\frac{f''}{2}+\frac{f'}{r}\Bigr),$$

$$\operatorname{Ric}_{22}=1-f-rf',\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{33}=\bigl(1-f-rf'\bigr)\sin^2\vartheta,$$

and all mixed components $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ with $a\ne b$ vanish.

**(c) Vanishing for the model.** For $f(r)=1-s/r$ one has
$\frac{f''}{2}+\frac{f'}{r}=0$ and $1-f-rf'=0$; consequently

$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=0,\qquad S=0,\qquad G_{ab}=0$$

at every point of every product chart, hence on all of $M$. In particular the
Schwarzschild exterior metric is a Ricci-flat metric, and $G=0$ holds as an
identity of smooth tensor fields.

**(d) The curvature does not vanish.** The model is not locally flat:
$R_{0101}=-s/r^3$ and $R_{2323}=rs\sin^2\vartheta$ are nonzero at every point
of every product chart, so the curvature tensor is nowhere zero even though
the Ricci tensor and the Einstein tensor vanish identically.

items.title: Orthonormal-frame curvature components and the Kretschmann scalar 12s^2/r^6 of the Schwarzschild exterior metric
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum of mass parameter $m_*$,
Schwarzschild radius $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$
([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), with curvature data as in
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-ricci-and-einstein-tensors]]. In every product chart
$(x^0,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$ define the frame field

$$e_{\hat0}:=f^{-1/2}\partial_0,\qquad e_{\hat1}:=f^{1/2}\partial_1,\qquad e_{\hat2}:=r^{-1}\partial_2,\qquad e_{\hat3}:=(r\sin\vartheta)^{-1}\partial_3,$$

and for the curvature tensor define the **frame components**

$$\hat R_{\hat a\hat b\hat c\hat d}:=g\bigl(R(e_{\hat c},e_{\hat d})e_{\hat b},e_{\hat a}\bigr).$$

Then:

**(a) The frame field.** $(e_{\hat0},e_{\hat1},e_{\hat2},e_{\hat3})$ is a
smooth $g$-orthonormal frame (tetrad field) on the chart domain, with
$g(e_{\hat a},e_{\hat b})=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{\hat a\hat b}$, and
$e_{\hat0}$ is future-directed timelike; it is a tetrad field in the sense of
[[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. It is not a coordinate frame.

**(b) Frame components.** The nonzero frame components, up to the
symmetries $R_{abcd}=-R_{bacd}=-R_{abdc}=R_{cdab}$ of
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]], are

$$\hat R_{\hat0\hat1\hat0\hat1}=\frac{f''}{2},\qquad \hat R_{\hat0\hat2\hat0\hat2}=\hat R_{\hat0\hat3\hat0\hat3}=\frac{f'}{2r},$$

$$\hat R_{\hat1\hat2\hat1\hat2}=\hat R_{\hat1\hat3\hat1\hat3}=-\frac{f'}{2r},\qquad \hat R_{\hat2\hat3\hat2\hat3}=\frac{1-f}{r^2},$$

with $f'=s/r^2$ and $f''=-2s/r^3$; all other frame components vanish.

**(c) Kretschmann scalar.** Define the smooth function
$K:=R_{abcd}R^{abcd}$ in the product chart, with indices raised by the
inverse metric. Then

$$K=f''^2+\frac{4(f')^2}{r^2}+\frac{4(1-f)^2}{r^4},$$

and for the model function $f=1-s/r$ this is

$$K=\frac{12s^2}{r^6}=\frac{48\,G_N^2m_*^2}{c^4\,r^6}.$$

The identity holds at every point of every product chart, so $K$ is the value
of a smooth scalar field on $M$. Since $r>s$ on $M$, one has
$0<K=12s^2/r^6<12/s^4$ at every point; as $r\downarrow s$ the expression has
the finite boundary value $12/s^4$, and the expression $12s^2/r^6$, read as a
function of $r>0$, grows without bound as $r\downarrow0$.

**(d) Scope.** The lemma computes curvature data of the exterior datum on
$r>s$. The limit $r\downarrow s$ is the boundary value on $M$ of the smooth
expression $12s^2/r^6$; no value of the metric at $r=s$ or at $r=0$ is used
or asserted here, those regions being outside the datum (the regular
continuation across $r=s$ is the separate extension lemma of this page).

items.title: Smooth horizon-crossing extension of the Schwarzschild exterior metric in the advanced chart
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum with Schwarzschild radius
$s>0$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$
([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]). Let
$M_{\mathrm{ext}}:=\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the product
smooth structure and let $(v,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$ be its product charts
([[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]]).
Define the **tortoise function**

$$r_*(r):=r+s\log\left|\frac{r}{s}-1\right|,\qquad r>0,\ r\ne s,$$

on each of the two intervals $(0,s)$ and $(s,\infty)$, and define the
**advanced-chart metric** $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ on $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$ by the
components

$$g_{\mathrm{ext}}=-f(r)\,dv^2+2\,dv\,dr+r^2\,d\Omega^2,$$

meaning the symmetric tensor with $g_{vv}=-f$, $g_{vr}=g_{rv}=1$,
$g_{\vartheta\vartheta}=r^2$, $g_{\varphi\varphi}=r^2\sin^2\vartheta$ and all
other components zero in every product chart. Then:

**(a) Smooth Lorentzian metric.** $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is a smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field on $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and at every point it is
nondegenerate with inertia $(3,1,0)$; hence $(M_{\mathrm{ext}},g_{\mathrm{ext}})$
is a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of
$r>0$, including $r=s$.

**(b) Time orientation.** The smooth vector field

$$N_{\mathrm{ext}}:=A(r)\,\partial_v-\partial_r,\qquad A(r):=\frac{f(r)+\sqrt{f(r)^2+4}}{2}>0,$$

satisfies $g_{\mathrm{ext}}(N_{\mathrm{ext}},N_{\mathrm{ext}})<0$ everywhere
and $g_{\mathrm{ext}}(N_{\mathrm{ext}},\partial_v)<0$ everywhere; hence
$N_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is a time orientation of $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and on the
region $r>s$ it determines the same future cone as the datum's time
orientation $\partial_v=\partial_0$.

**(c) Isometric embedding of the exterior.** The map
$\Phi:M\to M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, $(x^0,r,\omega)\mapsto(x^0+r_*(r),r,\omega)$
restricts to a diffeomorphism of $M$ onto the open subset $\{r>s\}$ of
$M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and $\Phi^*g_{\mathrm{ext}}=g$; the exterior datum is
therefore isometric to the region $r>s$ of the extension.

**(d) Vacuum and Kretschmann scalar of the extension.** The
metric-selected connection of $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ exists and is unique, its
Ricci tensor, scalar curvature and Einstein tensor vanish identically on
$M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and its Kretschmann scalar equals

$$R_{abcd}R^{abcd}=\frac{12s^2}{r^6}$$

on all of $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$. In particular the scalar is smooth and finite on
the horizon $r=s$, where it takes the value $12/s^4$.

**(e) The horizon is a null hypersurface.** The level set $\{r=s\}$ is a
smooth null hypersurface of $(M_{\mathrm{ext}},g_{\mathrm{ext}})$ whose null
generator direction is $\partial_v$; the frame of the advanced chart remains a
basis of every tangent space across $r=s$, and $\det(g_{\mathrm{ext}})=-r^4\sin^2\vartheta$
in every product chart.

**(f) Scope.** The extension constructed here is a smooth Lorentzian
manifold containing the exterior isometrically and regular across $r=s$; it
is not claimed to be maximal, and no uniqueness or global structure theorem
is asserted. The region $r\le0$ and the surfaces relevant to the Kruskal
model of this page are outside this statement.

items.title: The isotropic coordinate form of the Schwarzschild exterior metric and the isothermal radius shift
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum with Schwarzschild radius
$s>0$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$
([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]). Define

$$R:(s/4,\infty)\to(s,\infty),\qquad R(\rho):=\rho\Bigl(1+\frac{s}{4\rho}\Bigr)^{2},$$

and define the **isotropic radius** of a point $p\in M$ by
$\rho(p):=\rho_0(r(p))$, where $\rho_0:(s,\infty)\to(s/4,\infty)$ is the
inverse of $R$. Write $a:=s/(4\rho)$. Then:

**(a) The coordinate change.** $R$ is a smooth bijection with smooth inverse
and $R'(\rho)=1-\frac{s^2}{16\rho^2}>0$; its inverse is the smooth function

$$\rho_0(r)=\frac{(r-\tfrac{s}{2})+\sqrt{r(r-s)}}{2},$$

and the identity $R(\rho)=\rho+\frac{s}{2}+\frac{s^2}{16\rho}$ holds on
$(s/4,\infty)$.

**(b) The metric in isotropic coordinates.** In the chart
$(x^0,\rho,\vartheta,\varphi)$ obtained by replacing the coordinate $r$ by
$\rho(p)$ (so that $r=R(\rho)$ in the chart), the metric of the datum has the
components

$$g=-\Bigl(\frac{1-a}{1+a}\Bigr)^2 d(x^0)^2+(1+a)^4\bigl(d\rho^2+\rho^2(d\vartheta^2+\sin^2\vartheta\,d\varphi^2)\bigr),$$

that is, $g_{00}=-(1-a)^2/(1+a)^2$, $g_{\rho\rho}=(1+a)^4$,
$g_{\vartheta\vartheta}=(1+a)^4\rho^2$,
$g_{\varphi\varphi}=(1+a)^4\rho^2\sin^2\vartheta$ and all other components
zero.

**(c) Conformal flatness and the large-radius expansion.** On the region
where $(\rho,\vartheta,\varphi)$ are the standard spherical coordinates of
$\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, the spatial part of $g$ is the conformally flat
metric $(1+a)^4\,\delta$, with $\delta=d\rho^2+\rho^2(d\vartheta^2+\sin^2\vartheta\,d\varphi^2)$
in Cartesian coordinates $y=\rho\,\hat\omega$,
$\lvert y\rvert=\rho$. Moreover, for every $\rho_0>s/4$ there is a constant
$C(\rho_0)$ with

$$\Bigl|\bigl(1+\frac{s}{4\rho}\bigr)^4-1-\frac{s}{\rho}\Bigr|\le\frac{C(\rho_0)s^2}{\rho^2}\qquad\text{for }\rho\ge\rho_0,$$

and $\rho_0(r)=r-\frac{s}{2}+O(1/r)$ as $r\to\infty$; in particular $\rho$ is
not equal to the areal radius $r$.

**(d) The comparison warning.** The areal-radius coefficient
$f(r)^{-1}=(1-s/r)^{-1}=1+s/r+O(r^{-2})$ and the isotropic coefficient
$(1+s/(4\rho))^4=1+s/\rho+O(\rho^{-2})$ agree at leading order but differ at
next order when one substitutes $\rho=r$; consequently any comparison of the
Schwarzschild coefficients with weak-field coefficients stated in another
chart must first convert to a single chart by the explicit map $R$ and must
carry the resulting error terms. Matching coefficient functions in two
different radial coordinates without the conversion is not a valid
identification.

items.title: The static observer congruence of the Schwarzschild exterior model: unit field, integral curves, acceleration and clock-rate ratios
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum of mass parameter $m_*$
with Schwarzschild radius $s>0$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$
([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Define the
smooth vector field

$$n:=f^{-1/2}\,\partial_0=\Bigl(1-\frac{s}{r}\Bigr)^{-1/2}\partial_0$$

on $M$. Then:

**(a) Observer congruence.** $n$ is a smooth observer congruence on $M$ in the
sense of [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]: $g(n,n)=-1$ and
$g(n,N)<0$ at every point, so $n$ is a future-directed unit timelike field.

**(b) Integral curves.** For $p\in M$ in a product chart, write
$x(p)=(c_0,r_0,\vartheta_0,\varphi_0)$. The maximal integral curve of $n$
through $p$ is

$$s\mapsto\bigl(c_0+f(r_0)^{-1/2}s,\ r_0,\ \vartheta_0,\ \varphi_0\bigr)$$

on all of $\mathbb R$; it is the **static observer worldline** at radius
$r_0$, with constant spatial coordinates, and the chart coordinate $x^0$ runs
monotonically along it.

**(c) Proper time and clock rate.** Along each static observer worldline the
proper time $\tau$ is an affine function of the flow parameter, with
$\frac{d\tau}{ds}=\frac1c$, and

$$\Delta\tau=\frac{\sqrt{f(r_0)}}{c}\,\Delta x^0=\sqrt{f(r_0)}\,\Delta t,$$

where $\Delta x^0$ is the coordinate difference in metres between two events
of the worldline and $\Delta t=\Delta x^0/c$ is the same difference in
seconds. In particular the proper-time increment is strictly positive for
$\Delta x^0>0$, and it is smaller than $\Delta t$ at every finite radius
because $0<f(r_0)<1$.

**(d) Clock-rate ratio.** For two static observers at radii
$r_1,r_2\in(s,\infty)$ compared over the same coordinate interval
$\Delta x^0$, the proper-time increments satisfy

$$\frac{\Delta\tau_1}{\Delta\tau_2}=\sqrt{\frac{f(r_1)}{f(r_2)}}=\sqrt{\frac{1-s/r_1}{1-s/r_2}} .$$

**(e) Acceleration.** The acceleration field of the congruence is
$a:=\nabla_nn=\frac{f'(r)}{2}\,\partial_1=\frac{s}{2r^2}\,\partial_r$; it is
spatial, nowhere zero, and points in the direction of increasing $r$, so the
static observers are not geodesics.

**(f) Scope.** These are identities of the geometric datum. The reading of
$\tau$ as the time measured by an ideal clock and of the congruence as a
family of static observers belongs to the framework's postulates and is not
asserted here; no measurement and no comparison with any observed rate is
made.

items.title: Conserved quantities and equatorial radial reduction of timelike geodesics of the Schwarzschild exterior model
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum with $s>0$ and
$f(r)=1-s/r$ ([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a **future
timelike geodesic**, parametrized by proper time $\tau$, with tangent
$U=\gamma'$, so that $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ is future-directed
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[lem-gr-parallel-transport-and-geodesic-speed]] clause 3,
[[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]). Fix a product chart
$(x^0,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$ containing the image of $\gamma$ and write a dot
for $\frac{d}{d\tau}$. Define

$$e:=-g(U,\partial_0)=f\dot x^0,\qquad \ell:=g(U,\partial_\varphi)=r^2\sin^2\vartheta\,\dot\varphi .$$

Then:

**(a) Conserved quantities.** $\partial_0$ and $\partial_\varphi$ are Killing
fields of $g$, and $e$ and $\ell$ are constant along $\gamma$; moreover
$e>0$.

**(b) Equatorial reduction.** Suppose $\vartheta(\tau_0)=\frac{\pi}{2}$ and
$\dot\vartheta(\tau_0)=0$ at some $\tau_0\in I$. Then
$\vartheta(\tau)=\frac{\pi}{2}$ for all $\tau\in I$; the geodesic is
**equatorial**.

**(c) Radial reduction.** If $\gamma$ is equatorial, define the **effective
potential**

$$W_\ell(r):=f(r)\Bigl(c^2+\frac{\ell^2}{r^2}\Bigr).$$

Then the normalization identity

$$\dot r^2=e^2-W_\ell(r)$$

holds at every $\tau\in I$, and, given this identity, the $r$-component of the
geodesic equation is equivalent to the one-dimensional equation

$$\ddot r=-\frac12 W_\ell'(r),\qquad W_\ell'(r)=f'(r)\Bigl(c^2+\frac{\ell^2}{r^2}\Bigr)-2f(r)\frac{\ell^2}{r^3}.$$

**(d) Scope.** The reduction is local: it is stated on the interval $I$ on
which the geodesic stays in one product chart with $r>s$ and
$0<\vartheta<\pi$; no completeness, no extension of $\gamma$ beyond $I$, and
no statement about null geodesics is made. The quantities $e$ and $\ell$ are
constants of the given geodesic, not functions of the model.

items.title: Circular timelike geodesics, their radial-potential stability threshold, and the photon sphere at r = 3s/2
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum with $s>0$ and
$f(r)=1-s/r$ ([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), with
$f'=s/r^2$. Then:

**(a) Existence of circular timelike geodesics.** Let $r_0>3s/2$ and put

$$\ell^2:=\frac{c^2sr_0^2}{2r_0-3s}>0,\qquad e:=\Bigl(f(r_0)\Bigl(c^2+\frac{\ell^2}{r_0^2}\Bigr)\Bigr)^{1/2} =\frac{c(r_0-s)\sqrt 2}{\sqrt{r_0(2r_0-3s)}}>0 .$$

Then the curve $\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$ with chart components

$$x^0(\tau)=x^0_0+\frac{e}{f(r_0)}\tau,\qquad r(\tau)\equiv r_0,\qquad \vartheta(\tau)\equiv\frac{\pi}{2},\qquad \varphi(\tau)=\varphi_0+\frac{\ell}{r_0^2}\tau$$

is a future timelike geodesic of the datum, with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-c^2$
and with the conserved quantities $e=-g(\gamma',\partial_0)$ and
$\ell=g(\gamma',\partial_\varphi)$ of
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-timelike-geodesic-reduction]]; it is a **circular
orbit** at radius $r_0$. Its angular velocity in the coordinate $x^0$ is

$$\frac{d\varphi}{dx^0}=\frac{\ell f(r_0)}{r_0^2e} =\Bigl(\frac{s}{2r_0^3}\Bigr)^{1/2},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \Bigl(\frac{d\varphi}{dt}\Bigr)^2=\frac{G_Nm_*}{r_0^3},$$

$t=x^0/c$.

**(b) The circular-orbit condition is necessary.** Conversely, if
$\gamma:I\to M$ is an equatorial future timelike geodesic with
$r(\tau)\equiv r_0>s$ constant on an interval of positive length, then
$r_0>\frac{3s}{2}$ and its conserved angular momentum satisfies
$\ell^2=\dfrac{c^2sr_0^2}{2r_0-3s}$; in particular there is no timelike
circular geodesic with $s<r_0\le\frac{3s}{2}$.

**(c) Stability threshold of the radial potential.** Let
$W_\ell(r)=f(r)(c^2+\ell^2/r^2)$ and $V_\ell=\tfrac12W_\ell$ be the potentials
of the reduction, evaluated at the circular-orbit value
$\ell^2=c^2sr^2/(2r-3s)$. Then

$$V_\ell''(r)=\frac{c^2s(r-3s)}{r^3(2r-3s)},\qquad r>\frac{3s}{2},$$

so $V_\ell$ has a strict local minimum at the circular-orbit radius exactly
for $r>3s$, a strict local maximum exactly for $\frac{3s}{2}<r<3s$, and
$V_\ell''(3s)=0$; the radius $r=3s$ is the **innermost stable circular orbit
radius** of the restricted model in this potential sense.

**(d) The photon sphere at $r=3s/2$.** Let $\ell\neq0$ and put
$r_0=\frac{3s}{2}$ and $e_0:=\dfrac{\lvert\ell\rvert\sqrt{f(r_0)}}{r_0}=\dfrac{2\lvert\ell\rvert}{3\sqrt3\,s}>0$.
Then the curve with chart components
$x^0(\tau)=x^0_0+\frac{e_0}{f(r_0)}\tau$, $r\equiv r_0$,
$\vartheta\equiv\frac\pi2$, $\varphi(\tau)=\varphi_0+\frac{\ell}{r_0^2}\tau$
is a future null geodesic (a **null circular orbit** or **photon sphere**
orbit) with conserved quantities $e_0$ and $\ell$, and its angular velocity is

$$\frac{d\varphi}{dx^0}=\frac{\ell f(r_0)}{r_0^2e_0}=\operatorname{sgn}(\ell)\,\frac{\sqrt{f(r_0)}}{r_0},\qquad \Bigl(\frac{d\varphi}{dx^0}\Bigr)^2=\frac{f(r_0)}{r_0^2}=\frac{4}{27s^2}.$$

The **null effective potential** $W^{\mathrm n}_\ell(r):=f(r)\ell^2/r^2$
satisfies $(W^{\mathrm n}_\ell)'(3s/2)=0$ and
$(W^{\mathrm n}_\ell)''(3s/2)=-\dfrac{64\ell^2}{81s^4}<0$, so the photon-sphere
radius is a strict local maximum of the null potential.

**(e) Scope.** All statements are exact data of the restricted model: the
orbits are ideal geodesics of the metric on the exterior domain, the
stability claim is the sign of the second derivative of the stated potential,
and no claim is made about nonlinear stability, about orbital decay, about
observations or about the interior region. The case $r_0=s$ is excluded, and
the reduction is stated only where $r>s$.

Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 7 (7.47)-(7.48) and the following pages: the effective potential V(r) = (1/2)epsilon - epsilon GM/r + L^2/2r^2 - GML^2/r^3, the circular orbits and the innermost stable circular orbit at r = 6GM, printed pp. 174-177 (PDF pp. 181-184)

items.title: The Kruskal model datum: domain, implicit radial function, metric and time orientation
items.statement:
This item assumes the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through
the manifold-product and tangent-bundle suppliers cited below
([[def-countable-choice]]); no further choice principle is used.

**(a) Parameters.** Let $c>0$, $G_N>0$ and $m_*>0$ be the constants and mass
parameter of the Schwarzschild exterior datum, and put
$s:=2G_Nm_*/c^2>0$ ([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]] clause (a)). The
**Kruskal model datum of mass parameter $m_*$** is constructed from these
data as follows.

**(b) Domain and smooth structure.** Let
$\Omega:=\{(U,V)\in\mathbb R^2:UV<1\}$ and let
$\mathcal K:=\Omega\times S^2$, where $S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$ is the unit
Euclidean sphere, with the product smooth structure
([[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]],
[[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]]). It is a smooth four-manifold
without boundary. Write $U,V:\mathcal K\to\mathbb R$ for the first two
projections and $\iota:\mathcal K\to S^2$ for the third. A **Kruskal chart**
is a smooth chart $(U,V,\vartheta,\varphi)$ whose last two components form a
sphere chart of the standard spherical atlas, in which
$\gamma_{S^2}=\operatorname{diag}(1,\sin^2\vartheta)_{ij}$.

**(c) The radial function.** The datum carries a function
$r:\mathcal K\to(0,\infty)$, the **Kruskal radial function**, characterized by
the implicit relation

$$U\,V=-\Bigl(\frac{r}{s}-1\Bigr)e^{r/s}\qquad\text{at every point of }\mathcal K .$$

That for every $(U,V)\in\Omega$ there is exactly one $r(U,V)>0$ satisfying
this relation, and that $r$ is smooth, is not asserted here; it is proved in
[[lem-gr-kruskal-model-properties]] on this page, the justification record of
this definition. The value $r=0$ is not attained on $\mathcal K$, and
$r=s$ exactly on the axes $U=0$ or $V=0$.

**(d) The metric.** In every Kruskal chart define the component functions

$$g_{UV}:=g_{VU}:=-\frac{2s^3}{r}e^{-r/s},\qquad g_{\vartheta\vartheta}:=r^2,\qquad g_{\varphi\varphi}:=r^2\sin^2\vartheta,\qquad g_{UU}:=g_{VV}:=g_{U\vartheta}:=g_{U\varphi}:=g_{V\vartheta}:=g_{V\varphi}:=0,$$

where $r$ is the function of clause (c) evaluated at the point. These are the
components of a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field
$g_{\mathcal K}$ on $\mathcal K$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]):
the component functions are smooth on each chart domain by clause (c), and
chart independence follows on overlaps of sphere charts from the
transformation law of the round sphere metric, the $U,V$ coordinates being
common to all Kruskal charts. We write the informal display
$g_{\mathcal K}=-\frac{4s^3}{r}e^{-r/s}\,dU\,dV+r^2\,d\Omega^2$ with the
understanding that $dU\,dV$ denotes the symmetric product. That
$g_{\mathcal K}$ is a Lorentzian metric on $\mathcal K$ is proved, not
asserted, in [[lem-gr-kruskal-model-properties]].

**(e) Time orientation.** Define the field
$N_{\mathcal K}:=\partial_U+\partial_V$ on $\mathcal K$. Its component
expression is the same in every Kruskal chart; that it is a smooth timelike
field and hence a time orientation of $g_{\mathcal K}$ is proved in
[[lem-gr-kruskal-model-properties]].

**(f) Scope.** The datum is a geometric object: the definition asserts
nothing about whether $g_{\mathcal K}$ satisfies any field equation, about
its causal structure, about the maximality of the extension it provides, or
about nature. The comparison with the exterior datum, the vacuum property and
the causal structure are the content of the two following items on this page.
The region $\{UV=1\}$, where the implicit relation of clause (c) has no
solution with $r>0$, is not part of $\mathcal K$ and is not appended to it by
this definition.

S. M. items.title: Kruskal model properties: smooth radial function, Lorentzian metric, four-region isometries, vacuum and Kretschmann scalar
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal K=\{(U,V):UV<1\}\times S^2$, $r$, $g_{\mathcal K}$ and
$N_{\mathcal K}=\partial_U+\partial_V$ be the Kruskal model datum of mass
parameter $m_*$ and Schwarzschild radius $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2>0$
([[def-gr-kruskal-model-data]]). Then:

**(a) The radial function.** The function
$\varphi(r):=-(r/s-1)e^{r/s}$ is a smooth strictly decreasing bijection of
$(0,\infty)$ onto $(-\infty,1)$ with
$\varphi'(r)=-\frac{r}{s^2}e^{r/s}<0$; consequently the relation
$\varphi(r(U,V))=UV$ defines exactly one function
$r:\mathcal K\to(0,\infty)$, and this function is smooth. Moreover
$r(p)=s$ exactly when $U(p)V(p)=0$, and $r(p)\to0$ corresponds to
$U(p)V(p)\to1$; the value $r=0$ is not attained on $\mathcal K$.

**(b) Lorentzian metric and time orientation.**
$g_{\mathcal K}$ is a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on
$\mathcal K$ and is nondegenerate with inertia $(3,1,0)$ at every point; hence
$(\mathcal K,g_{\mathcal K})$ is a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$. The field $N_{\mathcal K}=\partial_U+\partial_V$
satisfies $g_{\mathcal K}(N_{\mathcal K},N_{\mathcal K})=-\frac{4s^3}{r}e^{-r/s}<0$
and is a time orientation.

**(c) The four regions and the isometries.** The set $\{UV\ne0\}$ has four
connected components. Let $r_*$ be the tortoise function of
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-extension-chart]] on the branch $r>s$ and define
$\Psi_+:M\to\mathcal K$ by
$\Psi_+(x^0,r,\omega)=\bigl(-e^{-(x^0-r_*(r))/(2s)},\,e^{(x^0+r_*(r))/(2s)},\,\omega\bigr)$.
Then $\Psi_+$ is a diffeomorphism of the exterior datum onto the component
$\{U<0,\ V>0\}$ and $\Psi_+^*g_{\mathcal K}=g$. Similarly, on the branch
$0<r<s$ with $r_*=r+s\log(1-r/s)$ the map
$\Psi_-(x^0,r,\omega)=\bigl(e^{(r_*(r)-x^0)/(2s)},\,e^{(r_*(r)+x^0)/(2s)},\,\omega\bigr)$
is a diffeomorphism of the domain $\mathbb R\times(0,s)\times S^2$ (carrying
the metric $-f\,d(x^0)^2+f^{-1}dr^2+r^2d\Omega^2$ with $f<0$) onto the
component $\{U>0,\ V>0\}$ and pulls $g_{\mathcal K}$ back to that metric. The
map $(U,V,\omega)\mapsto(-U,-V,\omega)$ is an isometry of $g_{\mathcal K}$
fixing $r$, exchanging the components $\{U<0,V>0\}\leftrightarrow\{U>0,V<0\}$
and $\{U>0,V>0\}\leftrightarrow\{U<0,V<0\}$; hence every component of
$\{UV\ne0\}$ is isometric to one of the two branches
$-f\,d(x^0)^2+f^{-1}dr^2+r^2d\Omega^2$ with $f=1-s/r$.

**(d) Vacuum and Kretschmann scalar.** The metric-selected connection of
$g_{\mathcal K}$ exists and is unique; its Ricci tensor, scalar curvature and
Einstein tensor vanish identically on $\mathcal K$, and its Kretschmann
scalar equals $R_{abcd}R^{abcd}=12s^2/r^6$ at every point of $\mathcal K$. In
particular the curvature invariant is smooth on $\mathcal K$ and grows
without bound as $UV\to1$ (that is, as $r\downarrow0$ at fixed angles), while
it equals $12/s^4$ on the axes $r=s$.

**(e) Scope.** The statements are geometric. No maximality of the extension,
no geodesic completeness, no uniqueness theorem and no global causal
statement beyond those proved here are asserted. The manifold
$\mathcal K$ contains a copy of the exterior datum and, on the components
with $UV>0$, points at $0<r<s$; the set $\{UV=1\}$ is not part of
$\mathcal K$.

P. K. Townsend, Black Holes, arXiv:gr-qc/9707012v1 (1997), section 2.3.2: the Kruskal metric (2.56) and the implicit relation (2.57), the extension of the range to U > 0, V < 0 and the four regions, printed pp. 20-22

items.title: The causal cone, the escape horizon and decreasing areal radius in the Kruskal model
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal K,r,g_{\mathcal K},N_{\mathcal K})$ be the Kruskal model datum of
mass parameter $m_*>0$ with Schwarzschild radius $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2>0$
([[def-gr-kruskal-model-data]], [[lem-gr-kruskal-model-properties]]), let
$(U,V,\vartheta,\varphi)$ be a Kruskal chart, let
$\gamma_{ij}$ be the round-sphere components in that chart, and define
$A:\mathcal K\to(0,\infty)$ by

$$A:=\frac{4s^3e^{-r/s}}{r},$$

so that in the chart $g_{UV}=g_{VU}=-A/2$, $g_{\vartheta\vartheta}=r^2$,
$g_{\varphi\varphi}=r^2\sin^2\vartheta$ and all other components vanish. For a
$C^1$ curve $\eta:J\to\mathcal K$ with $J$ a nonempty interval write
$\dot\eta=(\dot U,\dot V,\dot\vartheta,\dot\varphi)$ for its coordinate
components, and call $\eta$ **future-directed causal** when
$g_{\mathcal K}(\dot\eta,\dot\eta)\le0$ and
$g_{\mathcal K}(\dot\eta,N_{\mathcal K})<0$ at every parameter value. Then:

**(a) Causal cone criterion.** At every $p\in\mathcal K$ and for every
$X\in T_p\mathcal K$ with chart components $(X^U,X^V,X^\omega)$ one has:
$X$ is causal and future-directed if and only if

$$X^U\ge0,\qquad X^V\ge0,\qquad X^U+X^V>0,\qquad A(p)\,X^UX^V\ \ge\ r(p)^2\,\gamma_p(X^\omega,X^\omega),$$

where $\gamma_p(X^\omega,X^\omega)$ is the round-sphere squared norm of the
angular part. In particular every future-directed causal tangent has both
$X^U\ge0$ and $X^V\ge0$.

**(b) Monotonicity.** Along every future-directed causal $C^1$ curve the
functions $U$ and $V$ are nondecreasing, and along every past-directed causal
$C^1$ curve (where $g(\dot\eta,\dot\eta)\le0$ and
$g(\dot\eta,N_{\mathcal K})>0$) they are nonincreasing.

**(c) Radial null geodesics and their affine parameters.** For every
$(U_0,V_0,\omega_0)\in\mathcal K$ the curve $s\mapsto(U(U_0,V_0,\omega_0;s),V_0,\omega_0)$
defined implicitly by $\dfrac{dU}{ds}(s)=\dfrac{1}{A(U(s),V_0)}$, $U(0)=U_0$,
is a null geodesic of $g_{\mathcal K}$ on its maximal interval, with
$g(\dot\eta,\dot\eta)=0$ and affinely parametrized; the same holds for
$s\mapsto(U_0,V(s),\omega_0)$ with $\dfrac{dV}{ds}=\dfrac{1}{A(U_0,V(s))}$.
Both are future-directed, and $s$ is strictly increasing with $U$, respectively
with $V$, because $A>0$. Moreover $\partial_U r=-\dfrac{s^2Ve^{-r/s}}{r}$ and
$\partial_Vr=-\dfrac{s^2Ue^{-r/s}}{r}$ at every point of $\mathcal K$.

**(d) Escape horizon.** Call a future-directed causal $C^1$ curve $\eta$
**escaping to the right exterior** when there is a parameter value after which
$\eta$ stays in the open quadrant $\{U<0,\ V>0\}$ and
$r(\eta(t))\to+\infty$ as $t\to+\infty$ (a point with $U\ge0$ cannot reach the
quadrant $\{U<0,V>0\}$ at all, by (b), and this is the sense in which the
horizon is a one-way membrane here). Then:

1. no future-directed causal curve issued at a point $p$ with $U(p)\ge0$
   escapes to the right exterior;
2. every point $p$ with $U(p)<0$ admits such a curve: for
   $t>0$ the curve $\eta_p(t):=(U(p),\,V(p)+t,\,\omega(p))$ is a future-directed
   null geodesic (in the parametrization of (c)), it stays in
   $\{U<0,V>0\}$ for $t>1+|V(p)|$ and satisfies
   $r(\eta_p(t))\to+\infty$ as $t\to+\infty$.

Consequently the exact nonescaping set of the datum is $\{U\ge0\}$ with
boundary the null surface $\{U=0\}$, and the past-directed dual statement
singles out $\{V=0\}$ as the boundary of the region reachable from the left
exterior.

**(e) Decreasing areal radius.** If $U(p)>0$ and $V(p)>0$, then along both
future directions of the radial null geodesics of (c) through $p$ the function
$r$ is strictly decreasing: on $s\mapsto(U_0,V(s),\omega_0)$ and on
$s\mapsto(U(s),V_0,\omega_0)$ with $s$ increasing.

**(f) Scope.** All statements are geometric properties of the smooth Kruskal
datum on $\mathcal K$; no maximality, geodesic completeness or uniqueness is
claimed, the set $\{UV=1\}$ (where $r=0$) is not part of $\mathcal K$, and no
statement is made about the physical interpretation of any curve. The escape
notion of (d) is defined by the displayed conditions on $U,V$ and $r$ and does
not presuppose a conformal infinity.

items.title: The warped product of a two-dimensional Lorentzian base with a round sphere: Christoffel symbols and Ricci tensor
items.statement:
Let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be a nonempty open set with global coordinates
$y=(y^0,y^1)$ ([[def-interval]], [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]),
let $(q_{AB})$ be a smooth symmetric $2\times2$ matrix of functions on $V$
with

$$\Delta_q(y):=\det\bigl(q_{AB}(y)\bigr)<0\qquad(y\in V),$$

so that $q$ is a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $V$ whose value
at every point is nondegenerate with inertia $(1,1,0)$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]
clause (a), [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), and let $r:V\to(0,\infty)$ be
a smooth function. Indices $A,B,C,D$ run over $\{0,1\}$ and indices
$i,j,k,l$ over the sphere directions below. Define on $V$:

$$(q^{AB}):=(q_{AB})^{-1},\qquad \Gamma^A{}_{BC}:=\tfrac12\sum_Dq^{AD}\bigl(\partial_Bq_{DC}+\partial_Cq_{BD}-\partial_Dq_{BC}\bigr),$$

$$\operatorname{Hess}_{AB}r:=\partial_A\partial_Br-\sum_C\Gamma^C{}_{AB}\,\partial_Cr, \qquad \Delta_qr:=\sum_{A,B}q^{AB}\operatorname{Hess}_{AB}r, \qquad z:=\sum_{A,B}q^{AB}\partial_Ar\,\partial_Br .$$

Further define

$$R^A{}_{BCD}:=\partial_C\Gamma^A{}_{DB}-\partial_D\Gamma^A{}_{CB} +\sum_E\bigl(\Gamma^A{}_{CE}\Gamma^E{}_{DB}-\Gamma^A{}_{DE}\Gamma^E{}_{CB}\bigr), \qquad R_{ABCD}:=\sum_Eq_{AE}R^E{}_{BCD},$$

$$\operatorname{Ric}(q)_{BD}:=\sum_{A,C}q^{AC}R_{ABCD},\qquad S_q:=\sum_{B,D}q^{BD}\operatorname{Ric}(q)_{BD}.$$

Let $S^2:=\{y\in\mathbb R^3:\lVert y\rVert_2=1\}$ be the unit Euclidean
sphere with its induced smooth structure and round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$
([[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]],
[[ex-the-round-metric-on-the-sphere-as-an-induced-metric]]), let
$M:=V\times S^2$ carry the product smooth structure
([[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]]),
and let $(y^0,y^1,\vartheta,\varphi)$ be a **product chart** whose last two
components are the standard spherical chart of $S^2$ (so
$\gamma_{22}=1$, $\gamma_{23}=\gamma_{32}=0$, $\gamma_{33}=\sin^2\vartheta$).
On $M$ define the component functions of a symmetric covariant $2$-tensor
field $g$ by

$$g_{AB}:=q_{AB},\qquad g_{Ai}:=0,\qquad g_{ij}:=r^2\,\gamma_{ij} \qquad(A,B\in\{0,1\},\ i,j\in\{2,3\}),$$

where $\gamma_{ij}$ are the round-metric components of the sphere chart. Then:

**(a) The metric.** The assignments of the last display agree on the overlaps
of product charts and define a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field
$g$ on $M$; at every point $g$ is nondegenerate with inertia $(3,1,0)$, so
$(M,g)$ is a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(b) Christoffel symbols.** Let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection of
$g$, unique by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]
clause (b) ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), and let
$\Gamma^\mu{}_{\nu\rho}$ be its Christoffel symbols in a product chart. Then
the only nonzero symbols, beyond the displayed lower-index symmetry
$\Gamma^\mu{}_{\nu\rho}=\Gamma^\mu{}_{\rho\nu}$, are

$$\Gamma^A{}_{BC}\ \text{of the first display},\qquad \Gamma^i{}_{Aj}=\frac{\partial_Ar}{r}\,\delta^i{}_j,\qquad \Gamma^A{}_{ij}=-r\,q^{AB}\partial_Br\,\gamma_{ij},\qquad \Gamma^i{}_{jk}\ \text{the round-sphere symbols},$$

where the round-sphere symbols are $\Gamma^2{}_{33}=-\sin\vartheta\cos\vartheta$
and $\Gamma^3{}_{23}=\Gamma^3{}_{32}=\cot\vartheta$ with all other
$\Gamma^i{}_{jk}$ vanishing.

**(c) Ricci tensor.** With $\operatorname{Ric}$ the Ricci tensor of $\nabla$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (c)), in every product
chart

$$\operatorname{Ric}_{AB}=\operatorname{Ric}(q)_{AB}-\frac{2}{r}\operatorname{Hess}_{AB}r, \qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{Ai}=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=\bigl(1-z-r\Delta_qr\bigr)\gamma_{ij}.$$

**(d) Scope.** The statements are identities of the displayed component
functions in product charts and use no field equation, no vacuum condition and
no sign or positivity assumption on $s$; nothing is asserted about
completeness, geodesics, extensions or the physical reading of the coordinates.
The hypothesis $\Delta_q<0$ is used for nondegeneracy and inertia of $g$; it is
the only signature input.

items.title: Two-dimensional base identities for the warped spherical metric: pure-trace Ricci, the vacuum reduction and the extra Killing field
items.statement:
Let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be a connected nonempty open set, let $(q_{AB})$ be a
smooth symmetric matrix of functions on $V$ with $\Delta_q:=\det(q_{AB})<0$
everywhere, and let $r:V\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth; let
$\Gamma^A{}_{BC}$, $\operatorname{Hess}_{AB}r$, $\Delta_qr$, $z$, $R^A{}_{BCD}$,
$R_{ABCD}$, $\operatorname{Ric}(q)_{AB}$ and $S_q$ be the functions defined in
the statement of [[lem-gr-warped-spherical-christoffel-and-ricci]], so that all
index sums run over $\{0,1\}$. Assume in addition that $z\ne0$ everywhere on
$V$ and that the **warped vacuum equations**

$$\operatorname{Ric}(q)_{AB}=\frac{2}{r}\operatorname{Hess}_{AB}r, \qquad 1-z-r\Delta_qr=0 \qquad\text{on }V$$

hold, where the left-hand equation is the vanishing of the components
$\operatorname{Ric}_{AB}$ and the right-hand equation the vanishing of the
components $\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}$ of the warped metric of
[[lem-gr-warped-spherical-christoffel-and-ricci]] clause (c) (the mixed
components vanish there identically). Define the **base volume form** by

$$\varepsilon_{AB}:=\sqrt{-\Delta_q}\,\eta_{AB},\qquad \eta_{01}:=1,\quad\eta_{10}:=-1,\quad\eta_{00}:=\eta_{11}:=0,$$

and the **volume-form field** by

$$K_A:=\sum_B\varepsilon_{AB}\,\partial^Br,\qquad \partial^Br:=\sum_Cq^{BC}\partial_Cr,\qquad K^A:=\sum_Bq^{AB}K_B .$$

Then:

**(a) Pure trace in two dimensions.**
$\operatorname{Ric}(q)_{AB}=\tfrac12S_q\,q_{AB}$ and $S_q=\sum_{A,B}q^{AB}\operatorname{Ric}(q)_{AB}$
on all of $V$.

**(b) Vacuum reduction of the Hessian.** $\operatorname{Hess}_{AB}r=\tfrac12\Delta_qr\,q_{AB}$,
$\Delta_qr=\dfrac{1-z}{r}$ and $S_q=\dfrac{2\Delta_qr}{r}=\dfrac{2(1-z)}{r^2}$ on $V$.

**(c) Constancy of the mass parameter.** $\partial_Cz=\dfrac{1-z}{r}\,\partial_Cr$ for
$C=0,1$, hence $\partial_C\bigl(r(1-z)\bigr)=0$; consequently there is a
constant $s\in\mathbb R$ with

$$r(1-z)=s,\qquad\text{that is,}\qquad z=1-\frac{s}{r}\qquad\text{on }V .$$

**(d) The extra Killing field.** $K(r)=0$, $\sum_A K^A\partial_Ar=0$,
$\sum_{A,B}K^Aq_{AB}K^B=-z$, the field is nonzero at every point,
$\nabla_AK_B+\nabla_BK_A=0$ for the base connection $\Gamma^A{}_{BC}$ (so $K$
is a Killing field of $q$ in the sense of [[def-gr-killing-field]]), and the
fields $K$ and $\nabla r$ are pointwise linearly independent: the equalities
$\sum_A K^A\partial_Ar=0$, $\sum_{A,B}K^Aq_{AB}K^B=-z$ and
$\sum_{A,B}\partial_Ar\,q^{AB}\partial_Br=z\ne0$ show that neither field
vanishes and that the two are not proportional.

**(e) Explicit components of the Killing field.** With
$\lambda:=\sqrt{-\Delta_q}>0$ one has $K^0=-\dfrac{\partial_1r}{\lambda}$ and
$K^1=\dfrac{\partial_0r}{\lambda}$.

**(f) Scope.** The statements are identities of the displayed functions and
use only the two warped vacuum equations, the strict positivity of $r$ and the
hypothesis $z\ne0$; no field equation of the four-dimensional metric beyond
those two components, no global hypothesis on $V$ and no sign or physical
reading of $s$ is assumed. The constant $s$ is determined on the connected
set $V$; that it is the same constant for a larger region requires that region
to be connected as well.

items.title: Local Birkhoff theorem: a vacuum warped product with a round sphere factor is locally Schwarzschild with an extra Killing field
items.statement:
Let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be a connected nonempty open set with global
coordinates $y$, let $(q_{AB})$ be a smooth symmetric matrix of functions on
$V$ with $\Delta_q=\det(q_{AB})<0$ everywhere, let $r:V\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth
and let $z=\sum_{A,B}q^{AB}\partial_Ar\,\partial_Br$ be nonzero everywhere; let
$M=V\times S^2$ and let $g$ be the warped metric of
[[lem-gr-warped-spherical-christoffel-and-ricci]], whose Ricci tensor is given
there in clause (c) by $\operatorname{Ric}_{AB}=\operatorname{Ric}(q)_{AB}-(2/r)\operatorname{Hess}_{AB}r$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{Ai}=0$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=(1-z-r\Delta_qr)\gamma_{ij}$.
Assume the **vacuum condition**

$$\operatorname{Ric}(g)=0\qquad\text{on }M,$$

that is, the vanishing of all components of the Ricci tensor of $g$ in every
product chart. Then:

**(a) Mass parameter.** There is a constant $s\in\mathbb R$ such that
$z=1-\dfrac{s}{r}$ on $V$; equivalently $r(1-z)=s$.

**(b) Local Schwarzschild coordinates.** For every $p\in V$ there are an open
neighborhood $W\subseteq V$ of $p$ and a smooth function $T:W\to\mathbb R$ such
that $(T,r)$ is a smooth coordinate system on $W$, the vector field
$\partial_T$ coincides on $W$ with the volume-form field $K$ of
[[lem-gr-warped-base-vacuum-reduction]], and in these coordinates

$$q=-\Bigl(1-\frac{s}{r}\Bigr)dT\otimes dT+\Bigl(1-\frac{s}{r}\Bigr)^{-1}dr\otimes dr \qquad\text{on }W,$$

where $\bigl(1-s/r\bigr)^{-1}$ is the smooth function $1/z$ on $W$.

**(c) Local Schwarzschild form of the metric.** In the product chart
$(T,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$ over $W\times S^2$ the components of $g$ are

$$g_{TT}=-\Bigl(1-\frac{s}{r}\Bigr),\quad g_{rr}=\Bigl(1-\frac{s}{r}\Bigr)^{-1},\quad g_{\vartheta\vartheta}=r^2,\quad g_{\varphi\varphi}=r^2\sin^2\vartheta,$$

with all mixed components zero; that is,
$g=-\bigl(1-\frac{s}{r}\bigr)dT\otimes dT+\bigl(1-\frac{s}{r}\bigr)^{-1}dr\otimes dr+r^2\gamma_{S^2}$
on the chart domain.

**(d) Extra Killing field.** $\partial_T=K$ is a Killing field of $g$ on the
chart domain in the sense of [[def-gr-killing-field]]; it satisfies
$\partial_T(r)=0$ and $g(\partial_T,\partial_T)=-z=-(1-s/r)$. The metric
$g$ is therefore locally static on the chart domain, and the Killing field is
an additional symmetry not assumed among the hypotheses.

**(e) Scope.** The statement is local in $V$: a neighborhood of each point is
produced, and $s$ is a constant on the connected set $V$ but need not be
positive, need not be the same for a different connected component of a larger
region, and no asymptotic flatness, regular-center, completeness, maximality or
global uniqueness statement is made. The hypotheses $\Delta_q<0$ and $z\ne0$
are exactly those of the two quoted lemmas, and $r>0$ is used to divide by $r$.

items.title: The Schwarzschild exterior vacuum model: field law, static clock readings and the mass parameter
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]],
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]],
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] and
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] of the classical gravitational
framework, with the field law in its direct-equation presentation and the unit
conventions of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Let
$(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum of mass parameter $m_*>0$ with
Schwarzschild radius $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2$ and static congruence
$n=f^{-1/2}\partial_0$, $f(r)=1-s/r$
([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), and let the model's stress-energy
tensor be the vacuum prescription

$$T:=0\qquad\text{on }M,\qquad \Lambda:=0 .$$

Then all statements below are conditional deductions inside the model so
specified; they assert nothing about nature.

**(a) The Schwarzschild vacuum model.** $(M,g,N)$ satisfies the spacetime
postulate, $T=0$ is a smooth symmetric stress-energy tensor field on the
matter domain $M$ in the sense of [[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]], the
prescription is admissible, and the adopted field law
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ holds identically on $M$; in the
notation of [[pthm-gr-einstein-consistency-and-energy-conditions]] clause (d)
this datum is a vacuum solution of the field law, here read as a model of the
framework. The model is not locally flat: its curvature tensor is nowhere
zero, while its Ricci tensor and Einstein tensor vanish identically
([[lem-gr-schwarzschild-ricci-and-einstein-tensors]] clause (d)).

**(b) Static clock readings.** The integral curves of $n$ are the static
observer worldlines at constant radius $r_0$
([[lem-gr-schwarzschild-static-congruence-and-clock-rates]] clause (b));
adopting the clock rule of [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] clause (i),
the reading difference of an ideal clock carried along such a worldline
between two events whose coordinate times differ by $\Delta t$ is

$$\Delta\tau=\sqrt{f(r_0)}\,\Delta t=\sqrt{1-\frac{s}{r_0}}\;\Delta t,$$

so two static clocks at radii $r_1,r_2$ compared over the same coordinate
interval satisfy $\Delta\tau_1/\Delta\tau_2=\sqrt{f(r_1)/f(r_2)}$. The static
worldlines are not geodesics: their acceleration is
$a=\frac{s}{2r^2}\partial_r\ne0$, so the model assigns them to accelerated
(constrained) bodies and not to freely falling ones.

**(c) The mass parameter.** The parameter $m_*$ enters the model only through
$s=2G_Nm_*/c^2$ and through the quantities below; the framework reads $m_*$ as
the mass parameter of the model in kilograms
([[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]] clause (a),
[[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]] clause (a)):

1. Circular timelike geodesics with $r_0>\frac{3s}{2}$ have coordinate angular
   velocity satisfying $\bigl(d\varphi/dt\bigr)^2=\dfrac{G_Nm_*}{r_0^3}$
   ([[lem-gr-schwarzschild-circular-orbits-and-photon-sphere]] clause (a)),
   the Kepler-like law in which $m_*$ plays the role of the central mass;
2. in the isotropic chart of
   [[lem-gr-schwarzschild-isotropic-coordinate-form]] the leading far-field
   coefficient is
   $g_{00}+1=-\dfrac{s}{\rho}+O(\rho^{-2})=-\dfrac{2G_Nm_*}{c^2\rho}+O(\rho^{-2})$,
   the leading coefficient of twice a Newtonian potential $-\frac{G_Nm_*}{\rho}$
   in the framework's weak-field convention.

The reading is a statement about the model's own identities and the adopted
unit and weak-field conventions; no numerical value of $G_N$ or $m_*$, no
Newtonian source model realized by matter and no comparison with any reported
mass is asserted.

**(d) Scope.** The model is an idealized vacuum model of the framework, not a
claim about the actual universe: no observation, apparatus, calibration or
uncertainty is used, and no comparison with data is made. The datum solves the
field law with the chosen parameters $(m_*,\Lambda,T)=(m_*,0,0)$; other
solutions of the same field law exist and are not excluded, and the exterior
domain $r>s$ contains no horizon or interior region, whose treatment is the
subject of the extension and Kruskal items of this page. The physical
interpretation of coordinates, clocks and bodies remains the adopted one of
the cited postulates.

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 7 (7.29)-(7.34): the Schwarzschild metric with the parameter M, its interpretation as the conventional mass in the weak-field limit, and the static form of the solution, printed pp. 170-172 (PDF pp. 177-179)

items.physical_scope: Conditional model deduction inside the classical gravitational framework with the field law in its direct-equation presentation: the Schwarzschild exterior datum of mass parameter m_* > 0 with the vacuum stress-energy prescription T = 0 and zero cosmological parameter is a model of the framework satisfying the adopted field law; its ideal static clocks read the proper times of the static congruence, and the parameter enters the model through the Schwarzschild radius, the circular-orbit angular velocity and the leading far-field coefficient. Excludes: any claim that the model or its vacuum content is realized in nature, any empirical comparison (no observation, apparatus, calibration or uncertainty), non-vacuum matter, nonzero Lambda, the interior and horizon region (which belongs to the extension and Kruskal items of the page), distributional sources, and quantum effects. All conclusions are conditional on the adopted postulates.

items.title: Restricted redshift prediction of the Schwarzschild vacuum model: the observer-energy ratio between static observers
items.statement:
Adopt the Schwarzschild exterior vacuum model of
[[pthm-gr-schwarzschild-vacuum-model]]: the exterior datum $(M,g,N)$ of mass
parameter $m_*>0$ with $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$
([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), its metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), its static
congruence $n=f^{-1/2}\partial_0$
([[lem-gr-schwarzschild-static-congruence-and-clock-rates]]), and the light-ray
rule that ideal light rays are future null geodesics of $\nabla$
([[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] clause (iii)). Let $\eta:J\to M$ be
such a ray: a $C^1$ curve on an interval $J$ with tangent $W=\eta'$, $g(W,W)=0$
and $W$ future-directed ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). Let $s_E,s_R\in J$ with
$s_E<s_R$ and suppose $\eta(s_E)$ and $\eta(s_R)$ lie on static observer
worldlines of radii $r_E=r(\eta(s_E))$ and $r_R=r(\eta(s_R))$ with
$r_E,r_R\in(s,\infty)$. For each parameter value define the **observer energy
of the ray relative to the static observers** by

$$E(s):=-c\,g_{\eta(s)}\bigl(W(s),n(\eta(s))\bigr),$$

the value of the observer-energy definition of
[[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]] clause (a) for the unit
observer $n$. Then:

**(a) Constancy of the Killing pairing.** $\partial_0$ is a Killing field of
$g$ and the function $C:=-g_{\eta(s)}(W(s),\partial_0)$ is constant along $J$;
moreover $C>0$.

**(b) The observer-energy ratio.** $E(s)>0$ along the ray and

$$\frac{E(s_R)}{E(s_E)}=\sqrt{\frac{f(r_E)}{f(r_R)}}=\sqrt{\frac{1-s/r_E}{1-s/r_R}} .$$

**(c) Redshift parameter.** If the **redshift parameter** of the pair of events
is defined by $z:=\dfrac{E(s_E)}{E(s_R)}-1$, equivalently by
$1+z=E(s_E)/E(s_R)$, then

$$1+z=\sqrt{\frac{f(r_R)}{f(r_E)}} .$$

The ratio in (b) and (c) is unchanged if $W$ is replaced by $\mu W$ with a
nonzero constant $\mu$: a null ray determines its tangent only up to scale,
and only the ratio of energies is asserted. No observed wavelength, spectral
line, calibration or measurement enters the statement; the identification of
the ratio with a frequency ratio of an ideal ray is part of the framework's
geometric-optics reading, and moving observers require additional factors.

**(d) Scope.** The statement is a model prediction for the specified ideal
ray and the specified static observers; it asserts no redshift measurement and
no property of any real source, and it excludes non-geometric-optics
propagation, dispersion and any apparatus or analysis model.

items.title: Restricted geodesic predictions of the Schwarzschild vacuum model: circular free-fall orbits, the stability threshold and the photon sphere
items.statement:
Adopt the Schwarzschild exterior vacuum model of
[[pthm-gr-schwarzschild-vacuum-model]]: the exterior datum $(M,g,N)$ of mass
parameter $m_*>0$ with Schwarzschild radius $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2$ and $f=1-s/r$
([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), its metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and the
free-fall and light-ray rules of [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] (ideal
freely falling massive test bodies follow future timelike geodesics with
$g(U,U)=-c^2$ and proper time as affine parameter; ideal light rays are future
null geodesics). Then:

**(a) Circular free-fall orbits.** For every $r_0>\frac{3s}{2}$ the model
assigns to an ideal freely falling massive test body released on the circular
timelike geodesic of radius $r_0$ the worldline
$\gamma(\tau)=\bigl(x^0_0+\frac{e}{f(r_0)}\tau,\ r_0,\ \frac{\pi}{2},\
\varphi_0+\frac{\ell}{r_0^2}\tau\bigr)$ of
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-circular-orbits-and-photon-sphere]] clause (a), with
$e,\ell$ as there; it is a future timelike geodesic with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-c^2$
and proper time affine parameter, and its coordinate angular velocity satisfies

$$\Bigl(\frac{d\varphi}{dt}\Bigr)^2=\frac{G_Nm_*}{r_0^3}.$$

**(b) No circular free-fall orbit below the threshold.** If an equatorial
future timelike geodesic of the datum has $r\equiv r_0>s$ constant on an
interval of positive length, then $r_0>\frac{3s}{2}$; in particular no ideal
freely falling massive test body is assigned a circular worldline of radius
$s<r_0\le\frac{3s}{2}$.

**(c) Stability threshold of the restricted radial potential.** With
$W_\ell(r)=f(r)(c^2+\ell^2/r^2)$ the effective potential of the reduction and
$\ell^2=c^2sr^2/(2r-3s)$ the circular-orbit value, the second derivative of
$V_\ell=\frac12W_\ell$ at the circular-orbit radius is

$$V_\ell''(r)=\frac{c^2s(r-3s)}{r^3(2r-3s)},\qquad r>\frac{3s}{2},$$

so the potential has a strict local minimum at the circular-orbit value
exactly for $r>3s$ and a strict local maximum exactly for
$\frac{3s}{2}<r<3s$; the radius $r=3s$ is the innermost stable circular orbit
radius of the restricted model in this potential sense.

**(d) Photon sphere as an ideal light orbit.** The null circular geodesic of
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-circular-orbits-and-photon-sphere]] clause (d) at
$r=\frac{3s}{2}$ is assigned by the model to an ideal light ray, and along it

$$\Bigl(\frac{d\varphi}{dt}\Bigr)^2=\frac{4c^2}{27s^2} .$$

**(e) Scope.** All statements are conditional model predictions for ideal
test bodies and ideal rays in the exterior domain: no self-force, radiation
reaction, finite-size coupling, nonlinear orbital stability, orbit decay or
evolution, no interior or horizon region and no observation enters. The
stability claim of (c) is the sign of the second derivative of the stated
potential; the circular worldlines of (a) are geodesics of the model, and the
model assigns them to freely falling bodies only through the adopted
free-fall rule.

items.title: Horizon versus singularity in the Schwarzschild model: a chart breakdown, a smooth null surface and a curvature obstruction
items.statement:
The exterior datum of [[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]] is defined on the
open domain $r>s$ only. In its product charts the component
$g_{11}=f(r)^{-1}=(1-s/r)^{-1}$ diverges as $r\downarrow s$, and the chart
frame becomes degenerate in the same limit: $g(\partial_1,\partial_1)=f^{-1}$,
while the frame is $g$-orthogonal. This is a statement about the components of
the metric in one chart, not an invariant: the metric tensor field itself is
smooth and nondegenerate on $r>s$ ([[lem-gr-schwarzschild-extension-chart]]),
and component divergence in a chart is not a geometric obstruction.

Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), sections 6.1.2-6.1.4: the coordinate breakdown at r = 2GM, the null character of the horizon, the Kruskal extension and the statement that r = 0 is a genuine singularity while r = 2GM is not, printed pp. 236-249 (PDF pp. 243-256)

items.title: Scope and status of the spherical vacuum model page
items.statement:
- **The model.** [[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]] fixes the datum: the
  manifold $\mathbb R\times(s,\infty)\times S^2$, the smooth metric with
  components $-f,f^{-1},r^2,r^2\sin^2\vartheta$ in product charts, the time
  orientation $\partial_0$ and the parameters $c,G_N,m_*>0$ with
  $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2$. The components carry the unit readings of
  [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]; no numerical value of any
  constant is asserted.
- **The vacuum calculation.** [[lem-gr-schwarzschild-ricci-and-einstein-tensors]]
  computes the Christoffel symbols, the curvature, the vanishing Ricci and
  Einstein tensors and the nonvanishing curvature of the datum, and
  [[pthm-gr-schwarzschild-vacuum-model]] reads the result as a model of the
  framework's field law with $T=0$ and $\Lambda=0$, together with the model's
  static clock readings and the reading of the mass parameter.
- **Local uniqueness.** [[thm-gr-local-birkhoff-warped-product]] shows that a
  vacuum warped product with spherical orbits is locally of this form with an
  extra local Killing field, under the explicit hypotheses of that theorem;
  the conclusion is local and does not assert that every vacuum solution or
  every spherical vacuum region is an exterior region with positive mass.
- **Restricted predictions.** [[pthm-gr-schwarzschild-stationary-redshift]]
  and [[pthm-gr-schwarzschild-circular-orbit-predictions]] are conditional
  model predictions for ideal clocks, test bodies and light rays, using the
  adopted coupling rules of [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]]; they are
  not measurements and involve no apparatus model. The horizon and singularity
  distinctions are recorded in [[rem-gr-schwarzschild-horizon-and-singularity]].

items.title: Explicit isotropic-to-areal conversion and the second-order coefficient mismatch of the Schwarzschild exterior
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum with Schwarzschild radius
$s>0$, $f(r)=1-s/r$ and $g_{11}=1/f$
([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]],
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-metric-properties]]). Let

$$R(\rho):=\rho\Bigl(1+\frac{s}{4\rho}\Bigr)^{2},\qquad \rho>\frac{s}{4},$$

be the isotropic-to-areal radius map of
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-isotropic-coordinate-form]] and let
$\rho_0:(s,\infty)\to(s/4,\infty)$ be its inverse, so that the isotropic
coefficient of the spatial metric is the function
$\rho\mapsto(1+s/(4\rho))^{4}$ and the areal coefficient is
$r\mapsto(1-s/r)^{-1}$. Then the following explicit identities hold.

1. **Exact form and positivity.**
   $R(\rho)=\rho+\frac{s}{2}+\frac{s^{2}}{16\rho}$ and
   $R'(\rho)=1-\frac{s^{2}}{16\rho^{2}}>0$ on $(s/4,\infty)$; the inverse is
   $\rho_0(r)=\frac{(r-\frac{s}{2})+\sqrt{r(r-s)}}{2}$.
2. **Conversion and areal expansion.** With $\rho=\rho_0(r)$,
   $$\rho_0(r)=r-\frac{s}{2}-\frac{s^{2}}{16r}+O(r^{-2}),\qquad \frac{1}{\rho_0(r)}=\frac{1}{r}+\frac{s}{2r^{2}}+O(r^{-3}).$$
   The areal coefficient satisfies, exactly for $r>s$,
   $$(1-s/r)^{-1}=1+\frac{s}{r}+\frac{(s/r)^{2}}{1-s/r},$$
   so its expansion is $1+\frac{s}{r}+\frac{s^{2}}{r^{2}}+O(r^{-3})$.
3. **Isotropic coefficient after conversion.**
   With $\rho=\rho_0(r)$ one has
   $\frac{s}{4\rho_0(r)}=\frac{s}{4r}+\frac{s^{2}}{8r^{2}}+O(r^{-3})$ and
   $$\Bigl(1+\frac{s}{4\rho_0(r)}\Bigr)^{4}=1+\frac{s}{r}+\frac{7}{8}\frac{s^{2}}{r^{2}}+O(r^{-3}).$$
   Hence the two coefficients agree through first order and differ at second
   order by $\frac{1}{8}\frac{s^{2}}{r^{2}}$.
4. **Failure of the unconverted comparison.** Evaluating the isotropic
   coefficient at $\rho=r$ instead of at $\rho=\rho_0(r)$ gives
   $$\Bigl(1+\frac{s}{4r}\Bigr)^{4}=1+\frac{s}{r}+\frac{3}{8}\frac{s^{2}}{r^{2}}+O(r^{-3}),$$
   which differs from the areal coefficient of clause 2 by
   $\frac{5}{8}\frac{s^{2}}{r^{2}}$ at second order: the consistency of the
   leading Newtonian-type term is unaffected, but the comparison of
   coefficients in the unchanged chart is already wrong at relative order
   $(s/r)^{2}$.

items.title: Explicit static clock-rate ratios of the Schwarzschild exterior at r = 2s and r = 4s
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum with Schwarzschild radius
$s>0$, $f(r)=1-s/r$ ([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]) and static
observer congruence $n=f^{-1/2}\partial_0$
([[lem-gr-schwarzschild-static-congruence-and-clock-rates]] clause (a),
[[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]). By
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-static-congruence-and-clock-rates]] clause (c), a
static observer worldline at radius $r_0\in(s,\infty)$ has proper-time
increment

$$\Delta\tau(r_0)=\sqrt{f(r_0)}\,\Delta t=\sqrt{1-\frac{s}{r_0}}\;\Delta t$$

over a coordinate-time increment $\Delta t=\Delta x^0/c>0$. Then:

1. **Exact values at the two radii.** For $r_1=2s$ and $r_2=4s$ one has
   $f(r_1)=\frac12$, $f(r_2)=\frac34$, so
   $$\Delta\tau(r_1)=\frac{\Delta t}{\sqrt 2},\qquad \Delta\tau(r_2)=\frac{\sqrt 3}{2}\,\Delta t,\qquad \frac{\Delta\tau(r_1)}{\Delta\tau(r_2)}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}=\frac{\sqrt 6}{3}<1 .$$
2. **Monotonicity in the radius.** The function
   $r\mapsto\sqrt{f(r)}=\sqrt{1-s/r}$ is smooth and strictly increasing on
   $(s,\infty)$ with derivative
   $\frac{d}{dr}\sqrt{f(r)}=\frac{s}{2r^{2}\sqrt{f(r)}}>0$; consequently a
   static observer at the larger radius accumulates strictly more proper time
   over the same coordinate interval: $\Delta\tau(r_2)>\Delta\tau(r_1)$ for
   $s<r_1<r_2$, and the ratio of clause 1 is the exact instance at
   $(r_1,r_2)=(2s,4s)$.
3. **Large-radius limit.** $\sqrt{f(r)}\to1$ as $r\to+\infty$; the ratios
   $\Delta\tau(r_1)/\Delta\tau(r_2)$ are invariant under the common scaling of
   $\Delta t$ and tend to $1$ as
   $\min(r_1,r_2)\to+\infty$ with $r_2>r_1$.
4. **The static observers are accelerated.** At $r_1=2s$ the acceleration of
   the congruence is $a=\frac{s}{2r^{2}}\partial_r$
   ([[lem-gr-schwarzschild-static-congruence-and-clock-rates]] clause (e)),
   whose coefficient at $r_1=2s$ is
   $\frac{s}{2(2s)^{2}}=\frac{1}{8s}>0$: the observer held at $r_1=2s$ has
   nonzero acceleration pointing in the direction of increasing $r$, so it is
   not freely falling.

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 6.2: the gravitational redshift between static observers, printed pp. 249-251 (PDF pp. 256-258)

items.title: Explicit circular-orbit data of the Schwarzschild exterior at the ISCO radius 3s and the photon-sphere radius 3s/2
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum with Schwarzschild radius
$s>0$, $f(r)=1-s/r$ ([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), with the
circular-orbit data of
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-circular-orbits-and-photon-sphere]] and the radial
potential $W_\ell(r)=f(r)(c^{2}+\ell^{2}/r^{2})$ of
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-timelike-geodesic-reduction]] clause (c). Then the
following exact evaluations hold.

1. **The innermost stable circular orbit at $r_0=3s$.** With
   $\ell^{2}=\dfrac{c^{2}sr_0^{2}}{2r_0-3s}$ one has
   $\ell^{2}=3c^{2}s^{2}$, $e^{2}=\frac{8}{9}c^{2}$ and $e=\frac{2\sqrt2}{3}c$,
   and the second derivative of $V_\ell=\frac12W_\ell$ vanishes:
   $V_\ell''(3s)=\dfrac{c^{2}s(3s-3s)}{(3s)^{3}(6s-3s)}=0$. The circular
   angular velocity at this radius satisfies
   $\bigl(\frac{d\varphi}{dt}\bigr)^{2}=\dfrac{G_Nm_*}{(3s)^{3}}=\dfrac{c^{2}}{54s^{2}}$.
2. **The photon sphere at $r_0=\frac{3s}{2}$.** With
   $e_0=\dfrac{|\ell|\sqrt{f(r_0)}}{r_0}=\dfrac{2|\ell|}{3\sqrt3\,s}$ one has
   $f\bigl(\frac{3s}{2}\bigr)=\frac13$ and
   $\bigl(\frac{d\varphi}{dt}\bigr)^{2}=\dfrac{c^{2}f(r_0)}{r_0^{2}} =\dfrac{4c^{2}}{27s^{2}}$;
   the null potential $W^{\mathrm n}_\ell(r)=f(r)\ell^{2}/r^{2}$ has
   $(W^{\mathrm n}_\ell)'\bigl(\frac{3s}{2}\bigr)=0$ and
   $(W^{\mathrm n}_\ell)''\bigl(\frac{3s}{2}\bigr)=-\frac{64\ell^{2}}{81s^{4}}<0$.
3. **A stable comparison radius.** At $r_0=4s$ one has
   $\ell^{2}=\dfrac{c^{2}s\cdot16s^{2}}{8s-3s}=\dfrac{16}{5}c^{2}s^{2}$ and
   $V_\ell''(4s)=\dfrac{c^{2}s(4s-3s)}{(4s)^{3}(8s-3s)}=\dfrac{c^{2}}{320s^{2}}>0$,
   a strict local minimum: the two threshold values $3s/2$ (existence) and
   $3s$ (stability) separate the unstable circular orbits
   $\frac{3s}{2}<r_0<3s$ from the stable ones $r_0>3s$.
4. **Blow-up at the existence threshold.** As $r_0\downarrow\frac{3s}{2}$
   the required angular momentum diverges,
   $\ell^{2}=\dfrac{c^{2}sr_0^{2}}{2r_0-3s}\to+\infty$, so there is no finite
   angular momentum at the limiting radius; for $r_0\le\frac{3s}{2}$ no
   circular timelike geodesic exists
   ([[lem-gr-schwarzschild-circular-orbits-and-photon-sphere]] clause (b)).

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 7: the effective potential for Schwarzschild orbits, the innermost stable circular orbit at r = 6GM and the photon sphere at r = 3GM, printed pp. 179-184 (PDF pp. 186-191)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 6.3: circular orbits, the ISCO and the photon sphere of the Schwarzschild solution, printed pp. 252-258 (PDF pp. 259-265)

items.title: Explicit metric, orientation and curvature data of the advanced-chart extension at the horizon r = s
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum with $s>0$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$
([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), and let
$(M_{\mathrm{ext}},g_{\mathrm{ext}})$ with chart $(v,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$
and time-orientation field
$N_{\mathrm{ext}}=A(r)\partial_v-\partial_r$,
$A(r)=\frac{f(r)+\sqrt{f(r)^{2}+4}}{2}$, be the advanced-chart extension of
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-extension-chart]]. Write
$q_0:=(v_0,s,\vartheta_0,\varphi_0)$ for a point on the level set $\{r=s\}$
with $\sin\vartheta_0\ne0$. Then:

1. **Metric components and nondegeneracy at the horizon.** In the product
   chart, $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ has components
   $$g_{vv}=-f(s)=0,\qquad g_{vr}=g_{rv}=1,\qquad g_{\vartheta\vartheta}=s^{2},\qquad g_{\varphi\varphi}=s^{2}\sin^{2}\vartheta_0,\qquad \det(g_{\mathrm{ext}})=-s^{4}\sin^{2}\vartheta_0<0 .$$
   The two-dimensional block $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ in the
   $(v,r)$ directions is nonsingular with eigenvalues $+1$ and $-1$, and the
   angular directions are positive on $(0,\pi)$; hence $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is
   nondegenerate of inertia $(1,3,0)$ at $q_0$ with the same signature
   $(-,+,+,+)$ as in the exterior.
2. **Horizon generator and time orientation.** At $q_0$ the coordinate field
   $\partial_v$ satisfies $g_{\mathrm{ext}}(\partial_v,\partial_v)=-f(s)=0$
   and $g_{\mathrm{ext}}(\partial_v,\partial_r)=1\ne0$, so $\partial_v$ is a
   null direction tangent to the level set $\{r=s\}$ (the generator direction
   of clause (e) of the lemma). At $r=s$ the orientation field is
   $A(s)=\frac{0+\sqrt4}{2}=1$, so $N_{\mathrm{ext}}=\partial_v-\partial_r$,
   with
   $$g_{\mathrm{ext}}(N_{\mathrm{ext}},N_{\mathrm{ext}})=-2<0,\qquad g_{\mathrm{ext}}(N_{\mathrm{ext}},\partial_v)=-1<0 ,$$
   a unit-normalized timelike vector whose pairing with the generator is
   negative: $\partial_v$ is future-directed at the horizon.
3. **Finite curvature at the horizon.** By clause (d) of the lemma the
   Kretschmann scalar of $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ equals $12s^{2}/r^{6}$ on all of
   $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, so at $q_0$ its value is $12s^{2}/s^{6}=12/s^{4}$,
   finite and nonzero for every $s>0$.
4. **The chart component still diverges.** In the exterior product chart of
   the datum the component $g_{11}=f(r)^{-1}=(1-s/r)^{-1}$ diverges as
   $r\downarrow s$, while clauses 1 to 3 show that the metric, its
   orientation and the Kretschmann invariant at the same value $r=s$ are
   finite and nondegenerate in the extension. The divergence is therefore a
   property of the exterior chart's coefficient, not of the geometry at
   $q_0$.

references.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), sections 6.1.2-6.1.3: the Eddington-Finkelstein form, the horizon as a null surface and the finiteness of curvature invariants there, printed pp. 236-243 (PDF pp. 243-250)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 7: the tortoise coordinate, the advanced (ingoing) Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates and the regular behaviour of the metric at r = 2GM, printed pp. 184-187 (PDF pp. 191-194)

items.title: Explicit causal-cone and radial-derivative checks in the Kruskal model at the horizon point (U,V) = (0,1) for s = 1
items.statement:
Fix the Kruskal model datum of [[def-gr-kruskal-model-data]] with
Schwarzschild radius $s=1$, that is, with mass parameter
$m_*=\dfrac{c^{2}}{2G_N}$; this is a choice of one datum, not a measurement.
Let $r$, $g_{\mathcal K}$ and $N_{\mathcal K}=\partial_U+\partial_V$ be the
radial function, metric and time orientation of the datum
([[lem-gr-kruskal-model-properties]]) and let
$A=4s^{3}e^{-r/s}/r=4e^{-r}/r$ be the coefficient of
[[lem-gr-kruskal-causal-escape-and-trapping]] clause (a). Take the point

$$p_0:=(U,V,\omega)=(0,1,\omega_0)\in\mathcal K .$$

Then:

1. **The radius and the cone coefficient at $p_0$.** $U(p_0)V(p_0)=0$, so
   $r(p_0)=1=s$ (the point lies on the horizon) and
   $A(p_0)=4e^{-1}$. The future causal criterion of
   [[lem-gr-kruskal-causal-escape-and-trapping]] clause (a) at $p_0$ reads:
   $X$ is future-directed causal if and only if
   $X^{U}\ge0$, $X^{V}\ge0$, $X^{U}+X^{V}>0$ and
   $\frac{4}{e}\,X^{U}X^{V}\ \ge\ \gamma_{p_0}(X^{\omega},X^{\omega})$.
2. **Four explicit tangent vectors at $p_0$.**
   - $X_1=\partial_U+\partial_V$: $X_1^{U}X_1^{V}=1\ge0$ and
     $\frac4e\cdot1\ge0=\gamma(0,0)$, so $X_1$ is future causal; indeed
     $g_{\mathcal K}(X_1,X_1)=2g_{UV}=-A(p_0)=-\frac4e<0$, timelike.
   - $X_2=\partial_U$: $X_2^{U}=1$, $X_2^{V}=0$, so the inequality reads
     $0\ge0$ and $X_2$ is future causal; moreover
     $g_{\mathcal K}(X_2,X_2)=0$, so $\partial_U$ is future null at $p_0$,
     consistent with $\partial_U$ being tangent to the horizon generator.
   - $X_3=\partial_V$: likewise $g_{\mathcal K}(X_3,X_3)=0$,
     $g_{\mathcal K}(X_3,N_{\mathcal K})=-\frac{A(p_0)}{2}<0$, future null.
   - $X_4=\partial_U-\partial_V$: $X_4^{U}X_4^{V}=-1<0$ violates the
     criterion, and indeed $g_{\mathcal K}(X_4,X_4)=A(p_0)=\frac4e>0$,
     spacelike.
3. **Angular cut-off.** For
   $X_5=\partial_U+\partial_V+\omega$ with purely angular part $\omega$ one
   has $g_{\mathcal K}(X_5,X_5)=-\frac4e+\gamma_{p_0}(\omega,\omega)$, so
   $X_5$ is future causal exactly when
   $\gamma_{p_0}(\omega,\omega)\le\frac4e$. In the chart with round
   components $\gamma_{22}=1$, $\gamma_{33}=\sin^{2}\vartheta$, the choices
   $\omega=(1,0)$ and $\omega=(2,0)$ give $\gamma=1<\frac4e$ (causal) and
   $\gamma=4>\frac4e$ (spacelike), because $1<e<4$; the cut-off is the exact
   inequality, not a numerical approximation.
4. **Radial derivatives at $p_0$.** By clause (c) of the causal lemma,
   $\partial_Ur=-\dfrac{s^{2}Ve^{-r/s}}{r}$ and
   $\partial_Vr=-\dfrac{s^{2}Ue^{-r/s}}{r}$; at $p_0$ with $s=1$, $r=1$,
   $U=0$, $V=1$ this gives
   $\partial_Ur(p_0)=-e^{-1}<0$ and $\partial_Vr(p_0)=0$. The value
   $\partial_Ur(p_0)=-e^{-1}$ agrees with implicit differentiation of
   $UV=-(r-1)e^{r}$: at $(0,1)$ one has $V\,dU+U\,dV=-r e^{r}\,dr$, that is
   $dU=-e\,dr$, so $\partial_Ur=-e^{-1}$ and $\partial_Vr=0$.
   Consequently the areal radius decreases along the future null direction
   $\partial_U$ at the horizon, in accordance with the decreasing-radius
   clause of the causal lemma.

items.title: The exterior Schwarzschild charts do not cover the horizon-crossing extension: the regular horizon point (v, r) = (0, s)
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum with
$s>0$ and let $(M_{\mathrm{ext}},g_{\mathrm{ext}})$ be the horizon-crossing
extension of [[lem-gr-schwarzschild-extension-chart]]. Then every point of
$M_{\mathrm{ext}}$ lies in the image of the exterior datum under the embedding
$\Phi(x^{0},r,\omega)=(x^{0}+r_{*}(r),r,\omega)$, hence in the domain of some
Schwarzschild (product) chart of the datum; equivalently, every point added by
the extension is reached at a bounded value of the exterior coordinate
$x^{0}$."

The counterexample is the point

$$q_0:=(v,r,\vartheta,\varphi)=(0,s,\vartheta_0,\varphi_0)\in M_{\mathrm{ext}},\qquad \sin\vartheta_0\ne0,$$

on the level set $\{r=s\}$, and the following three facts refute both forms of
the statement:

1. $q_0\notin\Phi(M)$: the map $\Phi$ preserves the function $r$, so
   $r(\Phi(p))=r(p)>s$ for every $p\in M$, whereas $r(q_0)=s$.
2. $q_0$ is a regular point of a smooth Lorentzian manifold, not a boundary
   artifact: at $q_0$ one has $\det(g_{\mathrm{ext}})=-s^{4}\sin^{2}\vartheta_0\ne0$,
   the inertia is $(1,3,0)$, and the Kretschmann scalar is
   $12s^{2}/r^{6}=12/s^{4}$, finite and nonzero.
3. Every sequence $p_n\in M$ with $\Phi(p_n)\to q_0$ must have
   $r(p_n)\to s$ and exterior coordinate
   $x^{0}(p_n)=v_0-r_{*}(r(p_n))\to+\infty$; so the exterior coordinate
   $x^{0}$ is unbounded along the approach to $q_0$, and the second form of
   the statement ("bounded $x^{0}$") fails as well.
